test_title: Delhi Police Constable (Executive) 2023 - GK/CA (Held on: 30 Nov, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: gk
question: From which of the following countries did India adopt the ‘procedure established by the law’?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Japan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The term **"procedure established by law"** is derived from the Japanese Constitution, which India adopted during the drafting of its Constitution.
 
• The phrase is enshrined in Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, guaranteeing the protection of life and personal liberty.
 
• Unlike the "due process of law" adopted by the US, "procedure established by law" emphasizes adherence to the process defined by the legislature, irrespective of its fairness or reasonableness.
 
• The framers of the Indian Constitution deliberately chose this concept to avoid judicial overreach, ensuring legislative supremacy during the initial years post-independence.
 
• This concept highlights the importance of legislative procedures in ensuring legal compliance, even if it doesn't directly address the principles of justice or equity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Procedure Established by Law:**

 
 
• It means that a law duly enacted by the legislature or governing body is valid if it follows the correct procedure, even if it is unjust or unfair.
 
• The judiciary ensures compliance with the procedure but does not evaluate the law's moral or ethical aspects.
 
 
 
• **Due Process of Law:**
 
 
• Unlike "procedure established by law," this concept (used in the US Constitution) allows courts to assess both the procedural and substantive aspects of a law.
 
• It provides greater protection of individual rights by ensuring fairness, justice, and reasonableness in laws.
 
 
 
• **Article 21 of the Indian Constitution:**
 
 
• States that "No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law."
 
• This article has been interpreted expansively by the Supreme Court of India to include rights such as privacy, clean environment, and dignity.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Evolution in India:**
 
 
• Over time, the Indian judiciary has interpreted "procedure established by law" to incorporate elements of fairness, reasonableness, and justice, bringing it closer to "due process of law."
 
• The landmark case **Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978)** marked a significant shift in this interpretation.
